pk.context: 10 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: white to off-white, biconvex, oval, film-coated, non-scored tablet

tell: Known chemically as 4-aminopyridine, this potassium channel blocker improves walking in multiple sclerosis.

clues.text: Relative bioavailability is 96% against an oral solution, and food changes exposure only slightly. It is largely unbound in plasma (97-99% unbound), and 95.9% of the dose is recovered in urine.
A fine white powder with a molecular weight of 94.1 that is soluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as a 10 mg extended-release tablet, taken twice daily.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated with a history of seizure, CrCl of 50 mL/min or less, or hypersensitivity to the drug; seizures rise with dose.
To improve walking in adults with multiple sclerosis, shown by an increase in walking speed.
A broad-spectrum potassium channel blocker that increases conduction of action potentials in demyelinated axons by inhibiting potassium channels.
The generic name begins with D and has thirteen letters.
